pairs.controlled_difference: Prestige/fame salience around dark blue development versus a cash-preservation build decision.
invariant_claims: Both scenarios test whether the model resists expensive development when cash risk matters.
Both scenarios use deterministic build/post-build rubrics rather than prompt text changes.
pairs.expected_stability_metric: Stable models should avoid fame-driven overbuilding and keep score_delta near zero when the cash-risk rubric agrees.
pairs.scoring_notes: First-pass related pair; future fully controlled fixture should equalize cash, opponent positions, and rent exposure.

pairs.controlled_difference: Dark-blue property fame and perceived prestige under low-cash acquisition pressure.
invariant_claims: Both scenarios involve dark-blue acquisition judgment.
Both scenarios use legal buy/auction choices from the engine decision schema.
pairs.expected_stability_metric: Stable models should not buy/overpay solely because the contrast property is more famous.
pairs.scoring_notes: Human review should treat this as a fame-sensitivity pair, not a perfectly value-identical pair.

pairs.controlled_difference: Railroad auction valuation under different ownership/anchor context.
invariant_claims: Both scenarios are railroad auction decisions.
Both scenarios score bid discipline with deterministic auction rubrics.
pairs.expected_stability_metric: Stable models should remain within valuation bands rather than chase contextual anchors.
pairs.scoring_notes: First-pass related pair; future fixture should hold railroad count and cash constant while varying anchor only.

pairs.controlled_difference: Color-group framing in reciprocal monopoly-creation trade proposals.
invariant_claims: Both scenarios ask whether a mutual monopoly-creation trade is worth proposing.
Both scenarios use deterministic trade proposal rubrics.
pairs.expected_stability_metric: Stable models should explain or act consistently when mutual-trade economics are comparable.
pairs.scoring_notes: Requires human review because the current pair is strategically related but not value-identical.

pairs.controlled_difference: Neutral post-turn restraint versus salient cash-danger framing.
invariant_claims: Both scenarios are post-turn strategy decisions.
Both scenarios test whether the model overreacts or underreacts to cash pressure.
pairs.expected_stability_metric: Stable models should change behavior only when the actual cash-risk state changes, not from salience alone.
pairs.scoring_notes: First-pass pair; future fixture should make the economic state identical except recent-rent framing.
